headline: A 2022 law gives the government 10 years to bring criminal charges or civil cases against borrowers who committed fraud on Paycheck Protection Program loans.
what_it_does: The law sets a 10-year statute of limitations for fraud involving Paycheck Protection Program loans. A statute of limitations is the deadline for starting a case, so this sets how long after the fraud the government can still bring criminal charges or civil enforcement actions against a borrower. The summary provided does not describe further details such as penalties or reporting rules.

who_it_affects.group: Businesses that received Paycheck Protection Program loans
who_it_affects.how: Borrowers who committed fraud on these loans can face criminal charges or civil enforcement for up to 10 years after the fraud.
They have a longer window of 10 years to start cases involving PPP loan fraud.
